scenes.headline: How fframes renders a video frame by frame
scenes.sub: Each frame is an SVG tree from a Rust function.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Tamsin! In fframes a video is just a function from the frame index to one SVG tree. Let me show you how.

scenes.text: Each frame is an SVG tree returned by a Rust function, so the whole video is a pure function of the frame index.
scenes.mark: a pure function of the frame index
scenes.say: The idea: write the frame as an SVG tree in Rust. Nothing carries over between frames. The video is a pure function of the index.

scenes.title: From frame index to encoded file

steps.say: Each frame is an SVG tree, returned by a Rust function of the frame index.
The tree goes to Skia, which rasters it on the GPU.
Parts of the tree with no changing values are hashed once at compile time, and replayed instead of redrawn.
The painted frame goes straight to the linked encoder, no separate process, and out comes the file.

scenes.title: Every node, or only what moves

left.title: Redraw everything
left.say: The simple way rebuilds every node each frame, making its paths and paints from scratch.

right.title: Hash the static parts
right.say: fframes hashes the parts with no changing values once, paints them once, and replays them every later frame.

scenes.title: Skia on the CPU versus Remotion
scenes.note: one synthetic scene, no encoder, the GPU was skipped
scenes.say: On the repo's own scene, fframes on the CPU takes under four seconds for thirty frames. Remotion takes over two minutes.

scenes.label: faster than Remotion, this one scene
scenes.note: CPU versus CPU; the GPU, the headline feature, was skipped
scenes.say: That is thirty-one times faster. But it is C P U versus C P U. The GPU, the feature on the box, was never run.

scenes.text: A frame that is a pure function of its index is one a machine can test, diff and ship.

recap: A frame is an SVG tree from Rust
Static parts are hashed once and replayed
The speedup is one synthetic scene
scenes.say: To recap: a frame is an SVG tree from Rust, the static parts are hashed once and replayed, and that big speedup is a single scene.
